recipes.name: Picnic Marinated Summer Slaw
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Combine cabbage, bell pepper, cucumber, green onions, and tomato in a large bowl.
Combine sugar, oil, vinegar, salt, and black pepper in a saucepan over medium heat; cook and stir until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes. Cool marinade.
Pour marinade over cabbage mixture; stir to coat. Marinate slaw in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Picnic Marinated Summer Slaw
raw_recipe.description: This picnic marinated summer slaw recipe features a tangy, warm dressing that's poured over cabbage, cucumbers, and tomatoes for a cool picnic option.

review.reviewBody: This was a pretty simple recipe. I made a sugar free version and a couple other adjustments. I made the portion larger by adding broccoli slaw to the mix. For the marinade, I used Apple cider vinegar, grapeseed oil, stevia powder, sea salt, and fresh ground pepper. This is definitely something I'll make again!

This was very good for our camping trip. I made it ahead and put in a tight Tupperware container. Everybody raved about it, I did add in some celery seed since I really like that in coleslaw and used white wine vinegar. One thing I did was cut the sugar down by almost half, oil and vinegar down some also, it seemed like an awful lot for just 10 ounces, and glad I did, still a great amount of liquid and not too sweet.

I made this just as directed, except for the optional green pepper. At first I thought this was awesome, but after a couple of bites it started to turn my stomach because it was so sweet. I should have known better when I saw the 1/2 cup of sugar in the ingredients, but I gave it a shot anyways. I tried to remedy this by adding in some more salt & pepper and some basil - it helped a bit, but it was still not as palatable as I would hope for. I just personally am not a fan of sweet vinaigrette dressings. I would like to try this again though with some fresh summer veggies from the garden. Next time I think I will try it with apple cider vinegar, salt, pepper, and dill and omit the sugar. 
If you like sweet vinaigrette though, you're going to love this.

I tweaked the recipe a little, I added shredded carrots and fire roasted corn as well. I also split the dressing with apple cider vinegar instead of just white. I added a touch of mayonnaise to help give the slaw a creamy finish!

Recipe Group Selection: 21, June 2014 ~ Great slaw! I added the optional green pepper and used apple cider vinegar rather than white vinegar. Mine marinated for about 4 hours before dinner. It was delicious and we both loved it. I had a 16 oz. bag of slaw and measured out the 10 oz. After having dinner, there was enough dressing left with the remaining slaw that I added the last 6 oz. of cabbage. Served this with 'Cheddar Bacon Hamburger with Horseradish' and 'Awesome Red Pepper Hummus Dip' both from AR and fresh veggies and fruit.

This summer slaw is delicious! It has a sweet and sour taste, and is super easy too make! I added a bit less sugar then the recipe says, and a few adjustments on the vegetables. To add some more color to the slaw, add red peppers, and purple cabbage. Otherwise, everyone enjoyed this summer slaw!
If you pour the dressing hot over the slaw, this salad will keep in the refrig for weeks getting better by the day.
This slaw was hard to stop eating--it is so good. I used rice vinegar instead of basic white vinegar. Have since shared this recipe with others.

I followed recipe, but added a can of mandarin oranges and reserved half the juice to extend the dressing. I also added about 1/4 t of red chili pepper to give a slight kick. The crowd loved it! Fresh and light and crisp.

6.28.18 Knowing our personal taste, I cut the sugar in half, (actually used Truvia®), otherwise, followed the recipe. This was quick and easy to make. I love the fact that it’s one of those dishes that you can make early in the day and put in the fridge, making dinner prep easier, keeping me out of the kitchen during summer.

Light, crunchy and delicious! Followed recipe, using 12 oz of shredded cabbage with carrots and swapped Splenda for sugar. Dressing was perfect for this amount of ingredients. Marinated for 6 hours and it was excellent! Hubby thinks it would be great served on fish tacos..maybe I'll try that next time!

Easy recipe. As others stated, sweet and sour dressing makes this delicious. I honestly was skeptical, but pleasantly surprised how good and healthy this is. I made exactly as written. I did not cut down the sugar. I used fresh half of a cabbage that i shredded thin. Roma tomatoes and a regular cucumber that i chunked up. Would add carrots too…. cuz why not! I would make this as is and then next time do whatever adjustments you prefer.
This may be our favorite new summer salad!
this is so delicious. My family loved it. I'll definitely make again
I first made it with half the sugar and then made it with a third of the called-for amount of sugar and loved it! I had to drain it before serving and again before storing any leftovers.

This was a huge hit at our family picnic! I used a popular sugar substitute instead of sugar and no one knew till I told them. Even my picky teenage daughter went back for seconds - this recipe is a keeper!

The sugar caramalized so I assume that means I didn't stir enough. Or maybe didn't cook it long enough. I strained it out, poured the dressing, and then stirred in 4 packets of splenda. Turned out alright.
I used 1/4 cup of sugar. I used 4 green onions. It tasted fine. I will make it again.
Loved this!!! The only thing I changed was I didn't put the green pepper in it but used shredded carrots instead. My husband is picky and even he liked it!
This was my first slaw and it blew me away! Super easy to throw together and the flavors were awesome. Some reviewers said it was too sweet but I think it's the perfect amount of sweet.
